speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to understand the cause, please describe when the rash first appeared and if it is itchy. Have you noticed any new soaps, detergents, or fabrics you've been exposed to recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; since the rash has persisted for five months without complete resolution, has it spread to your trunk or lower extremities, and do you notice any specific patterns like blisters or scaling? Additionally, do you have any personal or family history of eczema or other allergic conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Atopic Dermatitis (Chronic Eczema). The chronicity (5 months), bilateral distribution, pruritus, and lack of systemic symptoms or new triggers strongly support a diagnosis of atopic dermatitis, likely exacerbated by environmental allergens or stress. No further tests are required for this clinical presentation.
